tagline: Nineteen miles along the bluffs, then north through the pass.
intro: West of Goleta the freeway narrows to an expressway and runs nineteen miles along the Gaviota Coast, often right above the shore, past bluffs, isolated beaches and terraced grassland. Three state parks are strung along it. At Gaviota the road turns sharply north and heads inland through Gaviota Pass, on the line of El Camino Real. Only the northbound lanes go through the tunnel. Southbound traffic keeps the old road.
At least fourteen Chumash villages once stood on this coast. In 1942 a Japanese submarine shelled the oil pier near Ellwood, and nobody was hurt.

moments.title: El Capitán State Beach
moments.text: Tide pools on the beach and sycamores and oaks in the campground. Monarch butterflies gather here in autumn to spend the winter.

moments.title: Refugio State Beach
moments.text: The Chumash village of Qasil stood on a bluff just east of here. It may have traded with Santa Cruz Island, and remains of boats have been found at the site.

moments.title: Gaviota State Park
moments.text: The park runs from the beach to the mountain crest, split by the pass, a deep canyon cut clean through. Sundowner winds are often at their most violent here, mostly in late spring.
